admission.justification: The mode rule spans dashboard overrides, provider-bound settings and host profiles, catalog default discovery, the create payload and receipt observation. Each location preserves its input or observation without replacing Paseo as the decision-maker.

applicability: New role-agent starts through the dashboard and the MCP role-start tools.
conditions: A host-profile mode applies to the provider named by that profile. A configured settings mode applies to its own settings harness.
The mode listing uses its fresh answer or last successful saved answer. An unanswered mode listing with no saved answer does not supply a default.
A known listing can canonicalize a matching mode to its identifier. A named mode absent from the listing, or supplied while the listing is unknown, reaches the host as named.

A role launch receipt records the host observation separately from a named launcher, profile or settings choice. For a host-default choice it also reports the observed mode as the value. The saved replay request retains the create payload.
exclusions: A dashboard modeId is a distinct field. Permission-bearing and unknown-bearing start-call feature values remain subject to the user-settings authority check.
Mode observation records what Paseo reports. It does not certify that Paseo always applies a named mode.
MCP role_start and role_start_set accept no permission-mode argument. A receipt-bound replay preserves the recorded choices instead of making a new selection.
statement: For a new role-agent start, an explicit dashboard permission mode precedes the applicable host profile and matching settings row. When none supplies a mode, the create request uses an advertised host default only for a known mode listing. Create omits modeId when no mode applies. Paseo decides which mode it can apply.
